originalTitle: Unemployed young people to join AI boot camps to get job-ready
summary: Pilot scheme will provide three weeks of training as part of UK government’s latest attempt to address Neets crisis
content: Young people out of work or at risk of unemployment in the UK are to join “AI boot camps” where they harness the technology to get a foothold in the workplace. The government’s latest attempt to address the crisis in Neets – young people not in work or education – involves turning to a technology that many view as a potential threat to employment. A pilot in north-west England will provide up to 70 people aged 16 to 21 with three weeks of AI training, including learning to build AI tools, understanding how businesses use AI and learning to use the technology responsibly. There will also be workplace skills training such as in using office IT systems and timekeeping. The government wants the majority of attenders at the boot camp to gain an apprenticeship at local businesses that have signed up, including the defence firm BAE Systems and the food company Heinz. Lisa Nandy, the digital, culture, media and sport secretary, said the scheme would “support young people at a crucial juncture in their lives”. The pilot will be used to refine an England-wide AI skills scheme due to roll out next summer. The boot camp will use AI tools from US tech firms including Microsoft, the ChatGPT developer OpenAI and Anthropic, the startup behind the Claude chatbot. Bouke Klein Teeselink, an academic at King’s College London and an expert on the impact of AI on work, said the boot camp was a “good idea in principle”. “What we need to do is make juniors more attractive to companies and one way to do that is make them more productive by teaching them how to do AI well,” he said. However, Teeselink said he was sceptical that a three-week programme would be enough to make teens “AI-ready”, because AI readiness required continuous learning and updating of skills. Fears of AI’s impact on jobs have focused heavily on school leavers and graduates because AI tools are viewed as capable of performing the “grunt work” that is typically set aside for workforce newcomers, with white-collar industries such as law, finance and marketing among the most vulnerable. This week Stanford University in the US flagged a decline in the employment of young workers in AI-exposed occupations such as software engineering and customer service. The UK’s AI minister, Kanishka Narayan, said the programme would give young people “the skills they need to thrive in the AI workplace”, amid signs of growing pressure on youth employment. The latest data, published in May, showed the number of young people aged 16 to 24 neither working nor learning surpassed 1 million for the first time since 2013, reaching 1.01 million in the three months from January to March. An interim report by the former Labour minister Alan Milburn, also published in May, warned that the figure could rise to one in six by 2031 and that Britain risked leaving behind a “lost generation” of young people ill-prepared for work. Last month Andy Burnham committed to cutting the number of Neets but declined to set a target deadline.
chineseTitle: 失业年轻人参加 AI 训练营，为就业做好准备
chineseSummary: 作为英国政府解决尼特人危机最新尝试的一部分，试点计划将提供三周的培训
chineseContent: 英国失业或面临失业风险的年轻人将加入“人工智能训练营”，利用该技术在工作场所立足。政府解决尼特族危机的最新尝试包括转向一种被许多人视为对就业构成潜在威胁的技术。英格兰西北部的一个试点项目将为最多 70 名 16 至 21 岁的人提供为期三周的人工智能培训，包括学习构建人工智能工具、了解企业如何使用人工智能以及学习负责任地使用该技术。还将提供工作场所技能培训，例如使用办公室 IT 系统和计时。政府希望训练营的大多数参与者能够在已签约的当地企业获得学徒期，其中包括国防公司 BAE Systems 和食品公司 Heinz。数字、文化、媒体和体育大臣丽莎·南迪表示，该计划将“为处于人生关键时刻的年轻人提供支持”。该试点项目将用于完善英格兰范围内的人工智能技能计划，该计划将于明年夏天推出。该训练营将使用美国科技公司的人工智能工具，包括微软、ChatGPT 开发商 OpenAI 和 Claude 聊天机器人背后的初创公司 Anthropic。伦敦国王学院的学者、人工智能对工作影响的专家布克·克莱因·提斯林克 (Bouke Klein Teeselink) 表示，训练营“原则上是个好主意”。他说：“我们需要做的是让初级人才对公司更具吸引力，而实现这一目标的方法之一就是通过教他们如何做好人工智能来提高他们的生产力。”然而，Teeselink 表示，他对为期三周的计划是否足以让青少年“为人工智能做好准备”持怀疑态度，因为人工智能准备需要不断学习和更新技能。人们担心人工智能对就业的影响
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
